specs.source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' #sys, the 'Fact card — replaces every "FACT: … *Source: …" paragraph' block; README.md §0.4 'Fact card'; operator ruling 2.4 (2026-09-07, UI discrepancy report)
notes: The expected values below are operator ruling 2.4 (2026-09-07), which is the latest binding statement on this part and states exact numbers: sourced = 2px solid #1A1A1A LEFT edge, 1px rgba(0,0,0,.12) on the other three sides, radius 0 8px 8px 0, white; inference = 1px DASHED rgba(0,0,0,.25) all round, background #FAFAF8, italic body; needs counsel = 2px solid #F97316 left edge, otherwise as sourced.

The artboard 00 markup differs from that ruling and is recorded here so the divergence is visible rather than silently resolved: sourced there is `background:#fff; border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.12); border-radius:8px; border-left:3px solid #5A5552; padding:12px 14px 12px 16px`; inference is `background:#F5F2EE; border:1px dashed rgba(0,0,0,.3); border-radius:8px`; counsel is the sourced box with `border-left:3px solid #F97316`. Where the two disagree the operator's ruling is used, per the ruling's own framing ('build against them, ask nothing').
The variants are addressed through the mount's `[data-audit]` wrappers, which carry no styling of their own; `> div` inside each is the FactCard's own root element.

notes: Values are read from the artboard markup, which the handoff makes the authority ('where README prose and a page artboard disagree, the artboard wins').

`grid-template-columns` is compared with one `*` token: getComputedStyle resolves the track list to USED pixel widths, so the `1fr` title track reports the container's leftover width and cannot be a design constant. Every fixed track is compared exactly. The mount places the row in a 778px box — the content column the frame produces at 1440 (README §0.3).
The artboard's `gap:0 14px` is compared as row-gap 0 / column-gap 14px, which is how CSSOM reports it.

specs.source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/README.md §0.3 'The frame'; 'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' page artboards (frame grid `252px 1fr`, content grid `padding:20px 40px 40px; grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) 300px; gap:28px`); operator rulings 4.2 (nav card top margin), 5.1 (section treatment), 5.2 (one coloured rule per screen), 2.2/2.3/3.1 (the forbid list)
notes: The mount is the REAL AppShell wrapping DashboardBrief and RegulationDetailSurface, so the nav card, the content column, the dashboard section cards, the detail header and the detail action row are all in ONE measured tree. Composing the two surfaces together is an audit fixture, not a claim the product renders them together.

Nav card top margin is expected at 20px per operator ruling 4.2 ('margin: 20px 0 16px 16px so it aligns with the content column's 20px top padding. Fix it in the frame, once'). The artboard markup still shows 16px; the ruling supersedes it.

Ruling 5.1 requires a 3px graduated rule ABOVE each section title (full card width, top edge, no radius, linear-gradient(90deg,#5A5552,#5A5552 22%,rgba(90,85,82,.18))) and NO line below the title. The rule is checked through the selector `[data-section-rule]`: the product gives that element no marker today, so the check reports NOT BUILT, which is the correct status and also states the selector contract a fix lane should build to.

Ruling 5.2's sitewide count ('one coloured rule per screen') cannot be counted reliably today: BandGradientRule renders an unmarked `div[aria-hidden="true"]`, and the four-band gradient is not distinguishable by computed style alone from the ImpactMeter ramp or the full MilestoneTimeline track, which are also green-to-red gradients at similar heights. This spec therefore checks the ONE permitted instance exactly (the nav card cap) and forbids a band-proportion rule inside a page masthead. Adding `data-band-rule` to BandGradientRule would make the sitewide count a one-line check; that is a recommendation for the fix lane, not a deviation.

children.name: nav card — band-proportion gradient cap (the ONE coloured rule, ruling 5.2)
children.note: README §0.2: 'The four-band gradient rule (3px, segment widths proportional to the live band counts) is the brand mark'. Ruling 5.2 keeps it in this one place sitewide.

children.name: content column — grid and padding (dashboard)
children.note: README §0.3: 'padding: 20px 40px 40px; grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) 300px; gap: 28px; align-items: start'. The dc.html page artboards carry the identical declaration.

children.name: section card — no line BELOW the title (ruling 5.1)
children.note: Ruling 5.1: 'Live 18a (border-bottom 2px solid #5A5552 under the text) is wrong: remove it... Section title itself: Anton uppercase, no divider, no underline.'

children.name: section card — the 3px graduated rule ABOVE the title (ruling 5.1)
children.note: Ruling 5.1: 3px, full width of the card, top edge, no radius, linear-gradient(90deg,#5A5552,#5A5552 22%,rgba(90,85,82,.18)). Applies to every panel/section card on every page.

children.name: section title type (ruling 5.1: Anton uppercase)
children.note: README type scale: 'Display: Anton, uppercase, letter-spacing:.04em — page titles (34/28), card titles (20)'. No per-context exception is stated.

children.name: detail title type
children.note: README §0.3 and the type scale: Anton uppercase, 28px on detail, letter-spacing .04em. Operator 1.2 named this element.

forbid.name: floating Ask AI button (bottom-right, every page)
forbid.reason: Operator 2.2: 'Remove the floating Ask AI button on every page (bottom-right). The masthead command bar is the ask. No floating control.' The text filter is needed because BackToTop.tsx carries the IDENTICAL `fixed bottom-6 right-6 z-40` class set, so the bare selector matches two controls stacked at the same coordinates. BackToTop is outside every ruling in the operator's list and is left exactly as it is; it is logged here as an observation, not a finding.

forbid.name: a second CommandBar inside the detail header
forbid.reason: Operator 2.3: 'Remove the inline Ask about this [regulation…] bar from every detail masthead. The action row follows directly below the workspace tags row.'

forbid.name: HeroPriorityDropdown in the detail action row
forbid.reason: Operator 3.1: 'Remove the Immediate ▾ dropdown from the regulation detail action row… Action row is exactly Export brief (primary) · Share · ☆ Watch · + Tag.'

forbid.name: a second '+ Tag' trigger in the under-title tag row
forbid.reason: Operator 3.2: 'The action-row + Tag is the only trigger. Applied workspace tags still render as a row under the title; that row displays tags, it does not carry the trigger.' NOTE: this selector matches the legitimate action-row trigger too, so a count of 1 is the target state and a count above 1 is the defect; read the count in the Measured column.

forbid.name: a band-proportion (coloured) rule inside a page masthead
forbid.reason: Ruling 5.2: the band-proportion gradient stays in ONE place sitewide (the nav card cap and its mobile equivalents). Every other 3px rule uses the dark grey gradation from 5.1.
